sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid kaba1281 (Kaba) and Keegan/Boyeldieu HAL records.
sources.note: Glottolog lists only Moser 2004/2003 as descriptive refs plus Djarangar 2000 (subclassification) and Ethnologue. Boyeldieu's SBB tone papers on HAL (e.g. 2000 'Identité tonale et filiation des langues sara-bongo-baguirmiennes', halshs-00331683) have no PDF deposited and are comparative tone studies, not stress descriptions.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. n.d. Sara-Bagirmi Bibliography (ms., Morkeg Books).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliography only; the only Kabba-specific works listed are Moser 2004 (LSAL 63) and Moser & Dingatoloum 2007 (Kabba-English-French Dictionary).

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. & Dandet Djibet Apollinaire. 2014. Lexique Kaba, 4th ed. Cuenca: Morkeg Books.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Introduction (1 page) refers phonology to Keegan (2014); tones marked on every word; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 2014. The Western Sara Languages (Ngambay, Kaba, Laga), 5th ed. Cuenca: Morkeg Books (Sara-Bagirmi Languages Project).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. p. 8: 'Tone (high, medium, low) is marked above all vowels and tone-bearing consonants'; pp. 13-17 syllable structure (CV/CVC) and vowel harmony; pp. 25-30 'Comments on the Phonology' of Kaba (consonants, vowel patterns, sound changes) — no statement on stress anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent hits only French glosses).
